what_its_for: Acebutolol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and irregular heartbeats (arrhythmias). Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by slowing your heart rate and making your heart work less hard.
how_to_take: Take acebutolol by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time(s) every day to keep a steady amount in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious heart problems.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you. A common starting dose for high blood pressure is 400 mg once a day or split into two doses (200 mg twice a day). For irregular heartbeats, doses may be higher. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store acebutolol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid standing up too quickly, especially when you first start this medication, as it may cause dizziness. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much. Do not take over-the-counter cold, allergy, or diet medicines without asking your doctor or pharmacist first, since some of these can raise your blood pressure or affect your heart rate. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: very slow or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath or wheezing, sudden weight gain or swelling in your legs or feet, severe dizziness or fainting, chest pain, signs of low blood sugar (if you are diabetic) such as shakiness without sweating, or a skin rash. Also call your doctor if you feel unusually tired or notice any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure, you may start to notice some effect within 1 to 2 weeks, but it may take several weeks to get the full benefit. For irregular heartbeats, your doctor will monitor your response. Even if you feel well, keep taking your medicine — high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and slow heart rate. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted. Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver issues. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as acebutolol can pass to the baby. Asthma or COPD: Use with caution — beta-blockers like acebutolol can tighten the airways. Tell your doctor if you have any breathing problems. Diabetes: This medicine can hide some signs of low blood sugar (like a fast heartbeat). Monitor your blood sugar closely and talk to your doctor.
